key_insight: Tabular foundation models perform best as a family, but tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive depending on the dataset and compute budget.
clinical_relevance: TabBioMed can inform model selection for biomedical prediction research, but the abstract does not establish clinical readiness or patient benefit.
method: Curate 94 public biomedical tabular datasets across eight domains.
Standardize dataset-aware preprocessing and evaluation for classification, regression, and multi-target tasks.
Compare 23 models spanning classical baselines, boosted trees, neural architectures, and tabular foundation models.
evidence_signal: Across 94 datasets and 23 models, predictive performance and computational trade-offs varied by data regime and task type.
watch_item: Benchmark leaders may not suit every deployment: model choice should account for dataset characteristics, training cost, and inference constraints.
paper_title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
